passage: It was the week after the singing competition, when Francis's voice cracked on the high note. At lunch, the boys at the corner table kept doing the crack, a squeak and then laughter, every time Francis walked past. I didn't want to make a speech. I'm not good at those, and speeches make things louder. So I just picked up my tray and sat down across from Francis, like I always had. I asked about the cricket score. Francis answered in a low voice, staring at the dal. The squeaks came twice more, then stopped. Maybe they got bored. Maybe it's less fun when the person isn't alone. Walking back to class, Francis said, "Thanks, Samir." I said, "For what? You still owe me the score." We both knew for what.

qa.q: What happened to Francis's voice at the singing competition?
qa.a: Francis's voice cracked on the high note.

qa.q: Why did Samir choose not to make a speech to the corner table?
qa.a: Samir felt awkward about speeches, which make things louder, and wanted to back Francis quietly instead.

qa.q: Which small choice made the difference at lunch?
qa.a: Sitting across from Francis as usual and talking about cricket, so Francis wasn't alone and the mocking lost its audience.

qa.q: What might "Thanks, Samir" tell us about how lunch felt for Francis?
qa.a: Francis was likely embarrassed by the squeaks but grateful not to face them alone, even though nothing was said out loud.

grounding: A student sees a classmate mocked at lunch and quietly sits with them instead of lecturing the mockers, and the teasing fades.

passage:
PE teacher's note, Class 9, Tuesday
During the relay, Ganga tripped at the handover and fell. A group near the stands started chanting "Ganga-flop" and filming on a phone. Before I reached them, Tushar had jogged over, offered Ganga a hand up, and walked with her to the water tap. He didn't say a word to the group, just stood beside her while she rinsed her grazed knee. The chanting fizzled out within a minute; there was no one left to perform for.
What I did next: I checked Ganga's knee and sent her to the sick room with Tushar. I spoke to the group about the chanting and had the video deleted in front of me. I've informed the class teacher and will call Ganga's parents this evening. I also told Tushar privately that I saw what he did.

qa.q: What did the group near the stands start chanting?
qa.a: "Ganga-flop."

qa.q: Why do you think Tushar said nothing to the group?
qa.a: He seemed to want to help Ganga rather than start a fight, trusting that standing beside her would matter more.

qa.q: Which of the teacher's follow-up steps protect Ganga most?
qa.a: Having the video deleted stops it spreading, and telling the class teacher and her parents means adults can keep watching out for her.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Ganga to have Tushar beside her at the tap?
qa.a: Ganga may have felt less alone and less humiliated, able to rinse her knee without facing the chanting by herself.

grounding: A teacher records how a student quietly helped a mocked classmate away from the chanting without confronting the group, and what the teacher did next.

passage:
Friday
Today in chemistry, Pema got the valency question wrong and Kunal said, loud enough, "Another genius answer from Pema," and his bench did slow claps. Pema went red to the ears. Sir just said "settle down". I didn't say anything to Kunal. What could I say that wouldn't make it bigger? But when the bell went, I waited at her desk and we walked out together, the long way past the library. She was quiet, then said, "They do this every day, Ira. I don't want to come to school." Her voice wobbled. I said I'd go with her to Ms Rao, the counsellor, right then, and we went. Ms Rao listened to both of us and said she'd speak to our class teacher before the day ended. Pema squeezed my hand at the gate.

qa.q: What did Kunal's bench do after his comment?
qa.a: They did slow claps.

qa.q: Why didn't Ira say anything to Kunal?
qa.a: Ira worried that anything said to Kunal would only make it bigger, so Ira chose to stay with Pema instead.

qa.q: When Pema said "I don't want to come to school", what choice did Ira make, and why was it right?
qa.a: Ira took Pema to Ms Rao, the counsellor, right away, so an adult who could act knew about the daily mocking that same day.

qa.q: What might walking the long way past the library have meant to Pema?
qa.a: It gave Pema a quiet moment with a friend after being humiliated, which may be why she felt able to say how bad things were.

grounding: A student walks a mocked classmate out of class without lecturing the mocker, and when the classmate reveals distress, takes her to the counsellor the same day.

qa.q: Where did Jahnavi say to wait?
qa.a: At the chemistry lab door.

qa.q: What was Ritu worried about before the end of school?

passage: The bus to the kasba school was late again, and the boys under the neem tree had found something to do. Karthik's sweater was his elder sister's old one, a faded rose colour, and Suresh kept calling him "Karthika" in a high voice while the others hooted. Karthik stared at the dust by his slippers. Nazia had been sitting on the low wall by the flour mill with her geography book. She didn't march over. She didn't call Suresh anything. She just picked up her bag, walked across, and sat down next to Karthik. "Did you finish the map question? I'm stuck on the rivers." He blinked, then pulled out his notebook. They bent over it together. Suresh tried once more, but nobody laughed this time, and he drifted off to throw pebbles into the canal. When the bus came, Karthik let Nazia climb up first, and took the seat beside her.

qa.q: What did Suresh call Karthik?
qa.a: "Karthika", in a high voice.

qa.q: What does Karthik staring at the dust by his slippers suggest about his feelings?
qa.a: It suggests he felt ashamed and alone, wanting to disappear while the boys hooted at his sweater.

qa.q: What did Nazia choose instead of confronting Suresh, and what did it change?
qa.a: She sat beside Karthik and asked about the map question, giving him company and something ordinary to do; with nobody laughing, Suresh gave up.

qa.q: How might Nazia feel about her small act afterwards?
qa.a: Nazia may feel quietly glad that simply sitting beside Karthik stopped the laughing, since nobody laughed when Suresh tried again.

grounding: A student sees Karthik mocked at the bus stop and quietly sits beside him with homework, lowering the temperature without scolding the teaser.
